# Research notes: front-month Brent (CBZ26) settlement on Oct 16, 2026 (compiled Oct 5, 2026)

## 1. Resolution source and contract status
- **Barchart page not readable:** the CBZ26 historical page and overview came back empty to our fetch tool on Oct 5, probably because the prices load by JavaScript. We could not quote Barchart's own figures. A Barchart search snippet showing "87.99, expires 10/30/26, 67 days away" is a stale cache from about late August, so ignore it.
- **CBZ26 stays front month through Oct 16:**
  - ICE rule: "Trading shall cease at the end of the designated settlement period on the last Business Day of the second month preceding the relevant contract month." That puts the Dec-26 expiry on **Fri Oct 30, 2026**. https://www.ice.com/products/219/Brent-Crude-Futures
  - The Nov-26 contract expired on Sep 30, 2026.
- **Latest Dec-26 settlement: $102.25 on Fri Oct 2, 2026**, down $0.06 on the day. We saw this only in search snippets, not by reading the pages.
  - Newsquawk: https://newsquawk.com/headlines/crude-wrap-wti-x6-settles-usd---brent-z6-settles-usd-
  - EnergyNow: https://energynow.com/2026/10/oil-ends-volatile-week-mixed-as-emergency-reserve-release-knocks-wti-lower-but-brent-holds-above-102/
- **Dec-26 closes in the days before (Investing.com, LCOZ6):**
  - Sep 30: $98.03. The same day the Nov contract expired at $103.50, so the drop between series is a roll gap, not a real price fall.
  - Oct 1: $102.31, up 4.4%, on news of a US aircraft-carrier deployment.
  - Sources: https://financefeeds.com/brent-crude-price-november-expiry-roll/ and https://www.investing.com/commodities/brent-oil-historical-data
- **Oct 5 intraday:** about $101.1–101.5, down roughly 0.9–1.1% on the day.
  - Oilprice.com showed Dec-26 with a session range of 101.02–103.40.
  - Sources: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil and https://oilprice.com/futures/brent/
  - The Oct 5 settlement was not yet available.
- **Curve:** steep backwardation.
  - Dec-26 to Jan-27 spread was about +$3.3 (Oct 5, oilprice.com).
  - Around Oct 1, Jun-27 was about $87 and Dec-27 about $81 (FinanceFeeds).
- **Metaculus "credible sources":** the FAQ page blocked our fetch, so we could not quote it. From memory, it means reputable public sources such as major news outlets, official publications and established data providers. If Barchart has no value, ICE, Reuters or Investing.com should qualify. Unverified.
- **Pre-opening data:** everything above happened before the question opened and serves as context only. The question resolves solely on the Oct 16 session.

## 2. Recent news and status quo
**Regime**
- The US/Israel–Iran war began around Feb–Mar 2026, and Brent peaked near $120 in March. The exact start date varies by source.
- The Strait of Hormuz is still disrupted, the US is enforcing a naval blockade of Iran, and the US military is now escorting ships through Hormuz.
- Brent is up about 54–55% year on year (Trading Economics, Oct 5).

**Front-month path (Wikipedia chronology and Al Jazeera)**

| Date | Brent | Event |
|---|---|---|
| Aug 7 | $83.55 | |
| Aug 20 | $93.73 | New Iran sanctions |
| Sep 9 | $101.21 | |
| Sep 17 | $104.82 | |
| Sep 28 | about $107–108 intraday | Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz |

- Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026%E2%80%932028_world_oil_market_chronology and https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/28/oil-prices-surge-after-trump-rejects-irans-plan-to-reopen-strait-of-hormuz
- Late September saw several daily moves of ±7–9% in the Nov contract: Sep 21 −7.35%, Sep 24 +8.64%, Sep 25 −7.30%.

**Bearish factors**
- **G7 stock release (announced around Oct 2–3):** 100M barrels of crude and diesel over about 4 months. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/3/g7-to-release-100-million-barrels-of-oil-and-diesel-will-it-curb-prices
- **Goldman (around Sep 30):**
  - Gulf exports were back to 23.3 mb/d in the last week of September, in line with the 2025 average.
  - Hormuz transits were 132 for Sep 21–27, compared with about 130 per day before the war.
  - Goldman sees the market roughly balanced.
  - https://boereport.com/2026/09/30/gulf-crude-oil-exports-return-to-2025-level-goldman-sachs-says/
- **Aramco** cut November prices to Asia to six-year lows.
- **US crude stocks** rose 0.92 mb in the week to Sep 25 (EIA, released Sep 30). https://boereport.com/2026/09/30/us-crude-stocks-rise-gasoline-and-distillate-inventories-fall-eia-7/

**Bullish factors**
- US–Iran talks are stalled; on Sep 30 Trump denied being willing to ease sanctions.
- The US is sending more aircraft carriers (Oct 1).
- The Houthis claim attacks on Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais (around Oct 4–5). Saudi Arabia has not confirmed damage.
- A Saudi-backed operation is under way near Bab el-Mandeb.
- China halted fuel exports (around Oct 2).
- Crude tanker rates are about $1.2M per day.
- Diesel hit a record $6.40/gal on Oct 1.
- IEA (Sep 11): stocks have drawn 507 mb cumulatively since February, and the Gulf recovery is pushed to 2027. https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-september-2026

**OPEC+**
- On Oct 4, the seven-country group held November output unchanged at 31.01 mb/d. https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/05/opec-keeps-november-oil-production-unchanged-at-31-01-million-bpd/
- The next meeting is Nov 1, outside the window.

## 3. Base rates and volatility
- **Implied volatility (OVX, a WTI-based measure):**
  - Sep 2026: low 44.42 (Sep 4), high 63.32 (Sep 14), close 52.24 (Sep 30). From a search summary; not checked on the page.
  - It peaked around 121 in early 2026. https://www.investing.com/indices/cboe-crude-oil-volatility-historical-data
- **Realized volatility:** roughly 45–60% annualized from Sep 7 to Oct 5 by our rough calculation. This is uncertain because of the roll and suspect data rows, such as an Investing.com row dated Sunday Oct 4.
- **Long-run norms (from general knowledge, unsourced):**
  - Brent typically runs about 25–35% annualized.
  - The standard deviation of a 2-week move is about 5–6% in calm periods.
  - Moves over 10% in two weeks occur in roughly 5–10% of windows in normal regimes, and returns have fat tails.
- **Illustrative 1-sigma ranges for 9 trading days, anchored at $101.5:**

| Annualized vol | 1σ over 9 days | 1σ range |
|---|---|---|
| 30% | ±5.7% | $95.8–107.3 |
| 40% | ±7.6% | $93.9–109.2 |
| 52% (current OVX) | ±9.8% | $91.5–111.5 |
| 60% (Sept realized) | ±11.3% | $90.0–113.0 |

**Caveats**
- Many figures come from search snippets of 2026-dated articles.
- Please verify the Oct 2 ($102.25) and Sep 30 ($98.03) Dec-26 settlements against ICE data.
- We could not confirm that Barchart's figures match ICE's exactly.

(a) **Time left:** The Oct 16 settlement is about 9 trading days away (as of Oct 5, 2026). The result will be known that evening.

(b) **If nothing changed:** CBZ26 was trading around $101–101.5 intraday on Oct 5, after settling at $102.25 on Oct 2. The status-quo outcome is about $101.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Prices have fallen from the late-September spike (above $116 spot, about $107–108 front-month intraday) as Gulf exports recovered and the G7 announced a 100M-barrel release. Extrapolating that drift points to the mid-to-high $90s by Oct 16.

  - The EIA projects about $90 for H2 2026.
  - Goldman sees $80–85 by year-end and a roughly balanced market.
  - Morgan Stanley sees about $100 for Q4.

(e) **Low scenario:** A US–Iran diplomatic breakthrough or easing of the Hormuz blockade, combined with the G7 release and Aramco's price cuts. That could knock out the risk premium and send Brent to the high $80s or below.

(f) **High scenario:** The Houthi attacks on Aramco are confirmed to have damaged Saudi capacity, Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb shipping is disrupted, or a US–Iran naval clash breaks out. Any of these could push Brent back toward $115–125.
